newsitem.title: UK: Mexico firms in strong Brady market.
newsitem.headline: Mexico firms in strong Brady market.

text.p: News that Mexico will redeem all its outstanding Aztec bonds early, pushed up the rest of the country's Brady bonds in a strong emerging debt market on Wednesdya.
The rise gave a nudge up to the rest of the Latin American Bradys, while East European debt also continued to rise.
On Tuesday, the Mexican government announcet said it would redeem at par the remaining $1.1 billion worth of the floating rate bonds, due in 2008.
The Aztec bonds, issued in 1988, were the prototype of what a year later became the Brady bonds and the solution to Latin America's huge foreign debt problem.
The Aztec bonds had become something of a special case.

The Mexican government has a call option to buy them back at par, at which the price was already close. Thus the stripped spread, to make up for the fact noone was prepared to buy the bonds above 100, had gone out of line with the rest of the Mexican bonds.
Stripped spreads for Aztecs are 517 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, compared to under 400 for Mexican Bradys.
Prices of Mexican Bradys rise around 3/4 of a point on the redemption news.
"It's another element boosting the market if only because some of the money will be reallocated into Bradys," West Merchant Bank economic adviser Peter West said.
Elsewhere, Russia continued to gently glide to new highs, touching 86-3/4 percent of face value for dollar Vneshekonombank paper.
There was little concern in the market over President Boris Yeltsin's expected cabinet reshuffle, even though there is speculation he may ditch his prime minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
Traders said that the market mood now was far more settled over the make-up of the government, with the assumption that the current policy of economic reform would remain a priority.
However, if Cheromyrdin does go, the market will be watching very closely who Yeltsin puts in his place.
Bulgaria continued its inexorable climb, but more and more traders are looking at chances to take profits after the bonds have risen more than 30 percent since the end of January.
"Why not do a little profit-taking? You are bound to get another chance to step into Bulgaria," Bank of America trader Brigitte Standing said.
